ai.title: Add requestId to read-files protocol
ai.summary: The `read-files` and `read-files-response` actions now include an optional `requestId` string to correlate requests and responses. `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` generates a compact ID for outgoing requests and validates it against incoming responses, falling back to file path equality for legacy clients. This change affects the WebSocket protocol in `common/src/actions.ts` and the npm client implementation in `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to look at your project files, the app now tags that request with a short reference number and waits for the file list to come back labeled with the same number. If a file list comes back without a matching number, the app can still pair it up by comparing file paths, so older versions of the tooling keep working. The result you see is just faster, more reliable file lookups without any duplicate or mismatched results.

ai.title: Restore TOOLRESULTMARKER in client.ts to skip file reads
ai.summary: TOOL_RESULT_MARKER reintroduced to prefix tool result payloads in npm-app/src/client.ts. Mechanism: marker signals client to skip reading files in subsequent requests. Scope: internal client logic only. Detail: applies to both JSON-stringified objects and plain string responses.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer tries to open and read files you've already seen in recent messages, so conversations that include screenshots or file previews load faster. When the assistant sends back a tool result, a hidden label tells the interface to skip re-fetching those files on the next turn. This only affects the internal client logic, so it's already live today for anyone using the app with file-reading capabilities enabled.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.165
ai.summary: Updated package version from 1.0.164 to 1.0.165. Change affects only `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: Your installed copy of the assistant advanced to a newer build (1.0.165), which pulls together several small improvements shipped over the previous week. If you install or update now, you get a tweaked landing screen plus a couple of behind-the-scenes fixes that make file replies and follow-up requests more reliable. Existing users who already upgraded earlier this week will notice nothing new, since those pieces are already on your system; this step mainly keeps new installs current with the latest bundled fixes.

ai.title: Plan summary replaced by clarifying questions
ai.summary: The post-plan continuation prompt in backend/src/main-prompt.ts now asks for 2-3 clarifying questions and the plan.md filename, replacing the previous brief summary instruction. This shifts the agent's behavior after plan creation from summarizing to seeking alignment on proposed changes. The CLI welcome message in npm-app/src/cli.ts was also slightly rephrased.

eli5.text: After the assistant creates a plan for you, it now asks 2-3 questions to check your understanding instead of giving you a brief summary. If you are signing up for a new account, the welcome message tells you to wait a moment while setup happens. This behavior is in place today when you interact with the assistant after a plan is generated.
